newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major, Blair trade insults on single currency.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major, Blair trade insults on single currency.

text.p: Labour's Tony Blair and Prime Minister John Major traded insults on Thursday over the decision by the ruling Conservatives to allow candidates to declare their opposition to a European single currency in election addresses.

Blair repeatedly accused Major during Prime Minister's questions in parliament of weakness while Major replied by accusing the Labour leader of trying to censor Labour candidates who tried to express their own views.

The clashes followed news that Conservative chairman Brian Mawhinney had promised not to edit the personal messages candidates include in their election addresses even if they say Britain should never abandon the pound sterling.

"Your weakness, your failure of leadership, are the reason your government is the incompetent mess that it is," Blair told Major, challenging him at least to urge his party colleagues to support his own "wait-and-see" line on the single currency.
Accusing Blair of being "plain silly", Major said many senior Labour figures were just as much against the single currency as some of his own supporters.
"You may ask your candidates to fib to the electorate, our candidates will set out their views," he said.
"What you are trying to do is to censor and smother what your own party stands for." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
